schema_gaps: The quantitative-result schema has no explicit inequality operator for MIC values reported as > or ≤. Boundary values are stored as estimates with effect_measure and tags preserving lower-/upper-bound semantics plus original_result_text.

The domain model is oriented toward primary clinical-result context; genomic lengths and sequence-identity magnitudes that do not naturally map to population/exposure/outcome are preserved in qualitative_result atoms with numeric values in canonical statements and tags rather than forced into quantitative_result.
extraction_limitations: This is a three-page short communication with one patient and one clinical isolate; the paper does not report treatment or patient-centered outcomes.
No supplementary material was present in the retrieved packet.
The polymicrobial specimen and absence of dog sampling limit causal and zoonotic inference; those boundaries are preserved rather than converted into reported facts.
